newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB SEES W. CANADA WHEAT CROP OF 21.6 MLN TONNES.
newsitem.headline: CWB SEES W. CANADA WHEAT CROP OF 21.6 MLN TONNES.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board said on Thursday that it was forecasting a wheat crop in western Canada this year of 21.6 million tonnes, down from 29.5 million last year.
"The decrease is attributed to reduced yields and a shift to canola and flaxseed," the CWB said in a statement.
Western Canadian durum production was forecast at 3.9 million tonnes, down from last year's 4.7 million tonnes.
Wheat production in China was put at 114 million tonnes, even higher than the record crop of 110 million tonnes in 1996-97.
"Farmers (in China) planted more wheat at the expense of cotton, rapeseed and peanuts," the CWB said.
The CWB also forecast world wheat production this year at 587 million tonnes, about four million tonnes more than in 1996.
